questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: A university in an English-speaking country. A bigger variety of interesting classes. Somewhere far away and vastly different from Denmark. A university with special flair for my field of studies, anthropology.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy, but improvements could be made.I recieved a lot of emails, it did feel like I was drowning in emails for a while. Fewer emails with more informations and HIGHLIGHTED deadlines would be perfect.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I think I could have sought out assistance, but I didn't need any. I did recieve help from their Housing services to find a dorm, but this I did before I arrived in Canada.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Dorms, one dorm particularly, where all international students lived together.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: A meal plan was available. I chose to cook myself, no kitchen appliances or utensils or anything were at the kitchen before I arrived. We did have a full kitchen with an oven, stove and a microwave.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Bring own stuff for kitchen. Make sure to get the bedding bundles, because you are not provided a pillow or a duvet or any bedding, so first night is uncomfortable otherwise.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It looked very institutional, but it was very safe, just not nice looking.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We had to go to a specific building on the other side of campus to registrer and get our house keys. However, they did provide free taxis for us to get to our dorm after. It was a slow process.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Don't know.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was very successful, I got the classes I wanted. I applied for pre-approval for 7 classes, I was approved for 6. I then applied for 4 classes at the university (equivalent to 30 ects), and I got all 4. I had no scheduling issues.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just follow the deadlines. In my expereince you'll get the classes you want, if you apply within the deadline ( social science faculty).

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy to follow the classes. I found my classes to be more interesting than the ones, I have had at KU. The grade is given based on multiple assignments, quizzes, mid-terms and final exams. This means the workload through the year is a little higher than at KU, however, the final exam season is way less stressful, because you secure marks through the year.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was pretty similar, I had less tutorials. I only had one weekly tutorial, and it was very easy to follow. My lectures were between 2 and 3 hours long, so same as KU or a bit longer. Some of the teachers spoke pretty fast, but the English is very easy to understand. I would say the style of teaching is quite similar to KU.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Language, Gender and Sexuality (anthro and linquistics)
Cultures of the Middle East (anthro)
Advertising and society (sociology)
Women and Third World Development (sociology)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Women and Third World Development was a very interesting class focused on inequality and gender in many different countries. The amount of reading for the class was fitting. The professor was pretty good. The grade depended on a mid-term, one 10-page assignment and a final exam. 
Language, gender and sexuality was also a very interesting course. It focused on gender and sexuality, whilst taking an anthropological perspective on the way we use language. A good fit, if you're interested in both anthropology and linquistics.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Food and activities were more expensive than I had expected. You can spend less or more than this. In Canada, they don't add tax to the price listed in stores. In Ontario you pay 13% tax. Some of the other provinces, you pay 5% instead. I didn't get a phone plan while there, I could use my Danish one still. But I heard from people, that it was quite expensive, the cheapest phone plans were around 30 cad (165kr. per month), but many were like 50 cad (275) for 20 GB. 
Nothing was less expected than I thought.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They had a lot. Some of them, you had to be fast, cause spots filled up quickly.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Outdoors club, global cafe, different sport clubs etc. Many clubs. Also a nice cafe on campus, where you could study or hang out. It transformed to a bar at night.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Just participate in a bunch.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I went to Banff during a break, which was amazing. Also Vancouver is really nice. Niagara falls is close by. Canada has a lot of natural parks, see as many as possible while the weather is still warm, seasons change fast.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be friendly. I met nice people in the classes I took and also at the dorm, where I lived. I also met people through people. The locals are pretty open and talkative.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Tips (15% is considered pretty low) is expected. Weed is legal, so you're not necessarily in a bad part of town, if it smells like weed. Bars close at 2, and you're not allowed to drink on the streets.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People are nice, it is common to say 'thank you', when you exit a bus. The nature is amazing.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Live on campus, it is close to downtown and to uni. You can get an app for some stores to collect points and get discounts. Make sure to plan weekend trips as soon as you can, time goes by fast, and public transportation isn't great, so trips require some planning and possibly renting a car.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are Facebook-groups for people attending universities, I texted with a couple of other Danes going to the same place as me. It was nice knowing someone already before arriving.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to live in and experience a different culture while taking classes I found genuinly interesting. Meeting new people from all over the world.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I don't know.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
